title: Same-looking curves, different physics
idea: Identify the mathematical object before comparing its shape.

scenes.script: These curves may look related. But what does each curve actually represent?
scenes.visual: Three original, separately labeled previews; no morph implying equivalence.

scenes.script: Start with the map w equals z squared. A straight grid line becomes a parabola. We have moved points into another plane; we have not drawn a force.
scenes.visual: Two distinct panels: z-plane x,y and w-plane u,v. Highlight x=1 and its mapped parabola. Mark origin as a critical point, not an angle-preserving example.

scenes.script: The real part, x squared minus y squared, can also serve as a local two-dimensional potential. Its contours are equipotentials; the field follows minus its gradient, crossing them at right angles away from the origin.
scenes.visual: Return to domain x,y, explicitly not output u,v. Dashed equipotential hyperbolas, solid field lines and labeled arrows. Exclude origin from orthogonality claim.

scenes.script: An ideal magnetic dipole is different again. Its three-dimensional field lines follow the magnetic field. This is an ideal model outside its source, not a simulation inside a real bar magnet.
scenes.visual: Original 3D dipole curves, visible x,y,z axes, z-aligned moment. Mask source neighborhood; truncate curves at mask, never connect through singularity. Show just two colored azimuthal planes.

scenes.script: Project two dipole curves onto a screen. Distinct depths can overlap. Turn the camera and they separate. The camera changed; the physical field did not.
scenes.visual: Orthographic camera first looking along y: phi=±pi/3 curves overlap in x,z. Rotate camera azimuth to pi/6, keeping all 3D points fixed. Keep projection warning and orientation axes visible.

scenes.script: Before comparing patterns, ask: a mapped grid, a potential contour, or a field line? Check the definition, dimensions, and equations. Resemblance alone proves no common physics.
scenes.visual: Return to the three object labels with definitions and a compact source card. No proof arrow to RH or NS. Offer prediction: which object is tangent to its field?
labels: NO RH OR NS RESEARCH CLAIM
